title: Bug: Cosmetic systemd [DEPEND] Dependency failed messages on warm-reboot
author: yanmarkman
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Low

### Description of the bug

After a successful SONiC warm-reboot, the serial console prints repeated [DEPEND] Dependency failed for systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service messages (~10 times).

Only visible on serial console.

The network stack, orchagent, and SONiC services start correctly.

This does not occur on cold reboot.

Impact: Cosmetic only — does not affect functionality.

Suggested action: 
Mask or suppress systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service during warm-reboot



### Steps to Reproduce

Run AMD64 until SONiC fully up
Use SHELL in the SERIAL-CONSOLE
apply:   warm-reboot 
After successful reboot wait for some minutes for the prints (see log below).

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

-

### Relevant log output

```shell
Sep 03 19:12:42 sonic systemd[1]: systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service: Job systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service/st
Sep 03 19:32:00 sonic systemd[1]: systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service: Bound to unit systemd-networkd.service, but unit i 
Sep 03 19:32:00 sonic systemd[1]: Dependency failed for systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service - Enable Persistent Storage i 
Sep 03 19:32:00 sonic systemd[1]: systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service: Job systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service/st 
Sep 03 20:20:58 sonic systemd[1]: systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service: Bound to unit systemd-networkd.service, but unit i 
Sep 03 20:20:58 sonic systemd[1]: Dependency failed for systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service - Enable Persistent Storage i 
Sep 03 20:20:58 sonic systemd[1]: systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service: Job systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service/st
...............
```

comments.author: cpackham-atlnz
comments.body:
I'm seeing the same thing now with the Trixie update on 202511.

I think it's due to code in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/master/files/image_config/midplane-network/systemd-networkd.override.conf which runs `bash /usr/local/bin/is-npu-or-dpu.sh` which will return non-zero for platforms without a DPU or NPU . I assume the logic is to let systemd-network manage the network for the DPU/NPU but stay out of the way for a regular switch.

As you say the impact is cosmetic but it is a bit jarring for anyone looking at the startup output.

comments.author: Bojun-Feng
comments.body:
I also encountered the same issue.

As @cpackham-atlnz mentioned, `systemd-networkd` is skipped on non-DPU/NPU hardware, but `systemd-networkd-persistent-storage` is still trying to bind to it.

I imagine this can be fixed by adding the same `ExecCondition=/bin/bash /usr/local/bin/is-npu-or-dpu.sh` override to persistent‑storage, so they both get skipped on non‑DPU/NPU platforms.

comments.author: cpackham-atlnz
comments.body: @Bojun-Feng I gave adding the same `ExecCondition` in an override for `systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service` but I still got the same behaviour.

comments.author: Bojun-Feng
comments.body:
> [@Bojun-Feng](https://github.com/Bojun-Feng) I gave adding the same `ExecCondition` in an override for `systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service` but I still got the same behaviour.

Hmm seems like the dependency check happens (and fails) before we ever check `ExecCondition`. Maybe we can dynamically mask `systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service` in systemd generators? Making a pull request to see if it works.

Theoretically the cleanest approach would be to resolve it at build time: `sonic_debian_extension.j2` already uses Jinja2 conditionals for platform-specific configuration. Unfortunately the Mellanox platform image might boot on either a standard switch or a smart switch, so we don't have sufficient information just from looking at the platform...

---

**Update:** Masking `systemd-networkd-persistent-storage` did work, but other dependent services (for example `systemd-networkd-wait-online`) still triggered similar errors.

Rather than masking each dependent service individually, it makes more sense to mask `systemd-networkd` itself. That addresses the root cause: once the main service is properly masked and skipped, its dependents won’t be started or checked at all.

Opened a new PR (https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/pull/25223) to mask `systemd-networkd` directly instead of masking the dependent services one by one.

Using a generator to mask the unit files earlier could be a reusable pattern for other components that need to be strictly disabled on specific platforms. Generators are late enough to have runtime information, but also early enough to ensure the masked components are completely ignored by the dependency tree.

linkedPullRequests.title: [systemd]: Mask systemd-networkd on non-smart-switch platforms
linkedPullRequests.author: Bojun-Feng
linkedPullRequests.body:
#### Why I did it

Fix #25091
Fix #24523

After a successful SONiC warm-reboot, the serial console prints repeated `[DEPEND] Dependency failed for systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service` and similar messages on non-smart-switch platforms. This is a cosmetic issue that does not affect functionality but is jarring for anyone monitoring startup output.

The root cause is that `systemd-networkd.service` uses an `ExecCondition` to skip execution on non-smart-switch platforms. However, its dependent services (`systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service`, `systemd-networkd-wait-online.service`) still attempt to start and fail with dependency errors.

#### How I did it

* Added `mask_networkd_for_non_smart_switch()` function to systemd-sonic-generator that creates a symlink to `/dev/null` for `systemd-networkd.service` when not on smart-switch platforms (DPU/NPU)
* The masking occurs at early boot during generator execution, before systemd loads unit files
* Masking systemd-networkd directly causes all dependent services to be automatically skipped by systemd's dependency resolution
* Added `validate_masked_services()` test to verify correct masking behavior across all platform configurations

#### How to verify it

1. Build a SONiC image with this change
2. Boot on a non-smart-switch platform (no DPU/DPUS in platform.json)
3. Perform a warm-reboot: `warm-reboot`
4. Monitor serial console output
5. Verify no "Dependency failed for systemd-networkd-persistent-storage.service" or similar messages appear

#### Description for the changelog

Mask systemd-networkd.service on non-smart-switch platforms to prevent dependency failure
